intro: A plate of nasi goreng mamak is about 700 kcal (estimate). Most of the calories come from the big portion of rice and the oil used when frying in a large wok.

breakdown.part: Chilli sauce, soy sauce and seasoning

variants.name: Nasi goreng mamak with telur mata (fried egg)
Nasi goreng mamak with extra chicken

diet: Yes, fried rice isn't off-limits. But a mamak plate usually has lots of rice and oil, and not much protein. If you're trying to lose weight, control the portion and add protein. Having it 1-2 times a week can still fit your calorie budget.
tips: Ask for less oil and half rice, most shops can do it.
Add chicken or a boiled egg instead of a fried egg.
Order fried veg or cucumber on the side to fill you up.

swap.name: Half white rice + ayam tandoori + vegetables
swap.why: You still eat rice at the mamak, but with less oil and much more protein.

faq.q: What's the difference between nasi goreng mamak and regular fried rice?
faq.a: Nasi goreng mamak is usually redder and spicier, made with chilli sauce, soy sauce, sometimes curry powder, and a bit of curry mixed in.

faq.q: Why is nasi goreng mamak always oily?
faq.a: It's cooked fast over high heat with enough oil so the rice doesn't stick and gets that 'wok hei' aroma.

faq.q: Is nasi goreng mamak okay for dinner?
faq.a: Sure, but if it's late at night, try a smaller portion so it's not too heavy before bed.
